title_original: Deadline’s Reviews Of This Week’s Box Office Openers: ‘Clayface’, ‘Wildwood’ & More
excerpt_original: Several buzzy films are premiering in theatrical release beginning Friday, October 23, the start of a big weekend at the box office. DC Studios’ Clayface starring Tom Rhys Harries as the Batman villain and shapeshifter will be on the big screen, as will Laika’s newest…

blocks.text: Several buzzy films are premiering in theatrical release beginning Friday, October 23, the start of a big weekend at the box office.

DC Studios’ Clayface starring Tom Rhys Harries as the Batman villain and shapeshifter will be on the big screen, as will Laika’s newest stop-motion animation feature Wildwood , based on the book by Colin Meloy, frontman of The Decemberists. And Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder’s You Can See Everything starring Elizabeth Holmes meets its wide window this week after a wildly successful limited opening earlier in the month.
Other titles debuting this frame include Wicker , Possible Love , A Talent for Murder , Sacha Baron Cohen’s Ali G: Who IZ I? and more.
Scroll down to find Deadline’s reviews for this week’s openers.

blocks.text: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Image Credit: Amazon MGM Studios / Everett Collection Release: Wide (October 23) Distributor: Amazon MGM Studios Director: Sacha Baron Cohen Screenwriters: Sacha Baron Cohen & Anthony Hines & Peter Baynham & Dan Swimer & Dan Mazer & Keisha Zollar Cast: Sacha Baron Cohen, Morgana Robinson, Marion Robinson, Alphja Miknas, Clive Russell, Stewart Rodeheaver Review date: October 22 Deadline’s takeaway: Sacha Baron Cohen obviously believes the moment is right to bring back his LOL OG as the world has only sunk further into the abyss since his last appearance. While the new film drifts from bit to bit, some straining for laughs, enough of it works to make this feel like vintage Baron Cohen daredevil comedy at the expense of the clueless. — PH RELATED: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen’s Signature Prankster Returns In Outrageous Form With Something To Offend Everyone

blocks.text: ‘Clayface’ Image Credit: Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection Release: Wide (October 23) Distributor: Warner Bros/DC Studios Director: James Watkins Screenwriters: Mike Flanagan & Hossein Amini Cast: Tom Rhys Harries, Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella, Eddie Marsan Original review date: October 21 Deadline’s takeaway: Whether you’re a comic book nerd or a horror junkie, Clayface is worth the price of admission for its genre-driven approach to a lesser-known character, hopefully serving as a roadmap for the DCU’s onscreen future. Just maybe brace yourself if you’re squeamish. — GG RELATED: ‘Clayface’ Review: DCU Molds Batman Villain’s Origin Story Into Fun, Scary Body Horror

blocks.text: ‘Klara And The Sun’ Image Credit: Sony / 3000 Pictures Release: Wide (October 23) Distributor: Sony Pictures Director: Taika Waititi Screenwriters: Taika Waititi and Dahvi Waller (based on the book by Kazuo Ishiguro) Cast: Jenna Ortega, Amy Adams, Mia Tharia, Natasha Lyonne, Aran Murphy, Steve Buscemi, Rachel House, Jesse Griffin Original review date: October 15 (London Film Festival) Deadline’s takeaway: Taiki Waititi should be a snug-as-a-bug fit for Kazuo Ishiguro’s dystopian — or is it? — 2021 novel, given the director’s affinity for a very particular and peculiar kind of reality-based cringe comedy. But Klara just doesn’t deliver on any of the fronts it promises. — DW RELATED: ‘Klara And The Sun’ Review: Taika Waititi’s Latest Is A Curiously Flat Dystopian Comedy-Drama – London Film Festival

blocks.text: ‘A Talent For Murder’ Image Credit: Bleecker Street/LD Entertainment Release: Wide (October 23) Distributor: Bleecker Street Director: Anton Corbijn Writer: Joanna Murray-Smith Cast: Helen Mirren, Alden Ehrenreich, Olivia Cooke, Juliet Stevenson, James Faulkner Original review date: September 15 (Toronto Film Festival) Deadline’s takeaway: Helen Mirren, playing wildly against type, is a revelation in this flawed but very entertaining two-hander, which belongs in the unique subgenre of literary biographies in which a cult author’s life is investigated through the highly specific prism of their work. — DW RELATED: ‘A Talent For Murder’ Review: Helen Mirren Is Mesmerizing As Tortured Genius Crime Writer Patricia Highsmith – Toronto Film Festival

Grant, Marli Siu, Nabhaan Rizwan, Gustav Lindh, Ella Bruccoleri, Ben Ashenden, Kiell Smith Binoe Original review date: October 22 Deadline’s takeaway: A hit at Sundance where it was picked up by Black Bear , this wry film from writer-directors Alex Huston and Eleanor Wilson is sexy and satirically funny, but also oddly haunting as a truly twisted fable that says its never too late to become your own best version of Cinderella. — PH RELATED: ‘Wicker’ Review: Olivia Colman And Peter Dinklage Turn Alexander Skarsgård Into A Sexy Basket Case In Comic Fable That’s Pure Delight

blocks.text: ‘Wildwood’ Image Credit: Courtesy of Laika Release: Wide (October 23) Distributor: Fathom Director: Travis Knight Screenwriter: Chris Butler (based on the book by Colin Meloy) Cast: Carey Mulligan, Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Jacob Tremblay , Angela Bassett, Mahershala Ali, Awkwafina, Maya Erskine, Jake Johnson, Charlie Day, Tom Waits, Richard E. Grant, Amanda Stenberg, Tantoo Cardinal, Len Cariou, Marc Evan Jackson Original review date: October 11 (London Film Festival) Deadline’s takeaway: The painstaking stop-motion animation process applied to a tale on a scale rarely seen on this level is a visual knockout, and the story is a compelling one focused on a scrappy young heroine determined to fight back and save her baby brother after he is harrowingly abducted from the streets of Portland by a murder of crows. — PH RELATED: ‘Wildwood’ Review: Carey Mulligan Leads Voice Cast Of Laika’s Ambitious And Visually Stunning Stop-Motion Fantasy Epic – London Film Festival

blocks.text: ‘You Can See Everything’ Image Credit: A24 / Everett Collection Release: Wide (October 23) Distributor: A24 Directors: Nathan Fielder, Lance Oppenheim Cast: Nathan Fielder, Elizabeth Holmes, Billy Evans, Christopher Abbott Original review date: September 7 (Telluride Film Festival) Deadline’s takeaway: The unusual (to say the least) documentary, which was shot in secrecy and runs nearly 3 hours, is unlike any I have ever seen in terms of pure access. Its title is appropriate: these people appear to hide nothing. — PH RELATED: ‘You Can See Everything’ Review: Shocking Elizabeth Holmes Documentary With Nathan Fielder Is Like No Other You Have Ever Seen – Telluride Film Festival

blocks.text: ‘Love Language’ Image Credit: SXSW Release: Limited (October 23) Distributor: Vertical Director-screenwriter: Joey Power Cast: Chloë Grace Moretz, Anthony Ramos, Manny Jacinto, Isabel May, Lukas Gage, Billie Lourd, Chloe Fineman, Zach Zucker, Morgan Jay, Bobbi Althoff, Marchánt Davis, Dan Perrault Original review date: March 17 (SXSW) Deadline’s takeaway: Love Language is a return to classic rom-com form, with heart and humor, as well as a talented ensemble cast that beautifully brings Joey Power’s script to life against a dreamy Chicago backdrop. — GG RELATED: ‘Love Language’ Review: Chloë Grace Moretz Leads Messy Love Triangle While Capitalizing On Untapped Wedding Vows Market — SXSW

blocks.text: ‘Possible Love’ Image Credit: Joo Jae-bum/Netflix Release: Limited (October 23) Distributor: Netflix Director: Lee Chang-dong Screenwriters: Lee Chang-dong and Oh Jung-Mi Cast: Jeon Do-Yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung, Cho Yeo-Jeung Original review date: September 6 (Venice Film Festival) Deadline’s takeaway: In some ways Lee Chang-dong‘s first film in eight years, which is South Korea’s official entry into the International Feature Film Oscar race , might remind you of the class divide in Bong Joon Ho’s Oscar-winning Parasite . But with a pandemic between that release and this one, Lee’s film carries a poignant subtext: a certain desire for love and longing in a world more split apart than ever, and one which for many seems like it all is out of reach. — PH RELATED: ‘Possible Love’ Review: Lee Chang -dong’s South Korean International Oscar Entry Is Powerful Story Of Class And Desire – Venice Film Festival
